name: NetSuite
tagline: Oracle's cloud ERP: general ledger, AR/AP, inventory, order management, and financial reporting for mid-market companies.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. NetSuite is quote-only: base license plus modules plus per-user seats, negotiated annually.

verdictSummary: NetSuite is not an app, it is a decade of accounting regulation compiled into software and then audited. The parts you can see, invoices, purchase orders, an item list, are the easy 5%. The parts that matter are multi-entity consolidation, multi-currency revaluation, revenue recognition under ASC 606, tax jurisdictions, period close with locked books, and an audit trail your external auditors will actually accept. An agent can absolutely give you a double-entry ledger in an afternoon, and for a solo operator or a one-entity shop that might genuinely be enough. For anything that files consolidated statements or gets audited, you are not building software, you are taking on personal liability.
coreLoopDIY: A local double-entry ledger with a chart of accounts, journal entries, invoices, bills, and a trial balance plus P&L and balance sheet you can export.
requirements: Somewhere to run it, a local machine is fine
An actual accountant to sign off on your chart of accounts
Discipline to never edit a posted entry
whatYouLose: Audit trail and period locking that auditors recognize without arguing
Multi-entity and multi-currency consolidation, including FX revaluation at close
Revenue recognition, deferred revenue schedules, and anything ASC 606 shaped
Sales tax and VAT determination across jurisdictions, plus filing-ready reports
Every integration your business already runs through it: payroll, banks, 3PL, CRM, the lot
Someone to blame, and to call, when the books are wrong in Q4
moatNotes: ERP switching costs are legendary for a reason: the data model has your entire operating history in it, and the implementation partner ecosystem exists because migrating out is a multi-quarter project with a project manager.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody buys NetSuite because it is pleasant. They buy it because an auditor, an investor, or a bank asked for financials that reconcile, and because thirty other systems already write into it. The cost of a bad close is higher than the license, and the license is already absurd. Once your controller, your tax filings, and your quote-to-cash flow live inside it, the only exit is a funded migration project.
notes: A ledger is a weekend; a close is not. The moat is compliance liability plus twenty integrations that already point at it.
prompt:
Build a local, single-entity double-entry accounting ledger. This is a bookkeeping tool for one small business, not an ERP.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.12, FastAPI backend, SQLite via SQLAlchemy.
- Server-rendered Jinja2 templates plus HTMX for interactivity. No React, no build step.
- Decimal arithmetic everywhere for money. Never float. Store amounts as integer minor units.
- Run with: uvicorn app.main:app --reload. Everything local, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Data model:
- Account: code, name, type (asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense), parent_id for a tree.
- JournalEntry: date, memo, reference, posted_at, period_id.
- JournalLine: entry_id, account_id, debit_minor, credit_minor.
- Period: year, month, status (open, closed).
- Contact: name, type (customer, vendor).
- Invoice and Bill: contact, issue_date, due_date, lines, status. Each posts a JournalEntry on approval.

Hard invariants, enforce in code and test them:
- Every entry must balance: sum of debits equals sum of credits, or the save is rejected.
- A posted entry is immutable. Corrections happen only via a reversing entry that links back to the original.
- No entry can post into a closed period.
- Closing a period is one-way through the UI.

Screens:
- Chart of accounts, editable tree.
- Journal entry form with dynamic lines and a live balance indicator.
- Invoice and bill entry with auto-posting to AR/AP.
- Reports: trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, general ledger per account, AR and AP aging. All with a date range and CSV export.

Seed a plausible small-business chart of accounts on first run. Ship a seed script with three months of fake transactions so the reports are not empty.

Explicitly out of scope, state this in the README: multi-entity consolidation, multi-currency, revenue recognition schedules, sales tax determination, payroll, inventory valuation, fixed asset depreciation, bank feeds. The README must also say in plain words that this output is not audit-grade and should not be the system of record for a company that gets audited.

Include pytest coverage for balance enforcement, period locking, immutability of posted entries, and that the balance sheet actually balances against the trial balance.
